summary: This is a JUnit test that creates a Thermostat set to a low temperature and checks that its status reports "Heating". It is the smallest possible test: one object, one expected answer.

lines.text: Brings in the @Test annotation from JUnit 5, which is how you mark a method as a test that the test runner should execute.
A static import lets you call assertEquals directly instead of writing Assertions.assertEquals every time, which keeps the test body short and readable.
Test classes conventionally take the name of the class under test with Test appended, so the pairing between Thermostat and its tests is obvious at a glance.
Marks the method below as a test case. Without this annotation JUnit ignores the method entirely.
The method name states the expected behaviour in words, so a failure report tells you what broke without you reading the code. Test methods need no return value and no public modifier in JUnit 5.
Sets up the scenario being tested: a thermostat reading 60 degrees, which is below the target and should therefore call for heat.
Compares the expected value with the actual one and fails the test if they differ. The expected value always comes first in assertEquals, which matters when you read the failure message.
